label: Couplings and Changes of Variables
notes: Welcome to Chapter 1, spanning printed pages 5 through 20. The single organizing idea is the coupling: a way of placing two probability measures on the same probabilistic stage so we can compare them. Everything later in optimal transport, transport plans, maps, distances, is a refinement of this one notion.

label: What Is a Coupling
notes: A coupling glues two measures into a joint law whose projections recover each one. Stress that couplings always exist because the product measure is one, so the coupling set is never empty. This non-emptiness is exactly what makes the Kantorovich relaxation a well-posed minimization rather than a possibly infeasible problem.

label: Marginals and Transport Plans
notes: Here the coupling becomes a transport plan: pi of dx dy is how much mass leaves a region of x and arrives in a region of y. The marginal constraints are conservation laws, total mass out equals mu, total mass in equals nu. The heatmap with edge histograms is the picture students should carry forward.

label: Three Classic Couplings
notes: Survey the canonical couplings before formalizing any one. The independent coupling spreads mass with no correlation; the deterministic coupling concentrates all mass on a graph; the monotone coupling on the line sorts mass increasingly. Each answers the same marginal constraints differently, which is the whole point of studying the coupling set.

label: The Independent Coupling
notes: The product measure is the maximum-entropy coupling: knowing x tells you nothing about y. Emphasize it as the baseline of zero structure against which every optimal coupling is a departure. Its density factorizes, so the joint heatmap is an outer product of the two marginal profiles, visibly rank one.

label: Deterministic Couplings and Maps
notes: A deterministic coupling lives on the graph of a map T, so randomness in y is entirely determined by x. This is the Monge picture: no splitting of mass. Make clear that not every pair of measures admits such a map, which is precisely why Kantorovich relaxed maps to plans.

label: Pushforward and Change of Variables
notes: The pushforward records where T sends mass: the measure of a target set equals the source measure of its preimage. For densities this becomes the change-of-variables formula with a Jacobian factor. Walk through why the determinant appears, it is the local volume distortion of the map.

label: The Monge-Ampere Relation
notes: When the transport map is a gradient of a convex function, the density constraint becomes a Monge-Ampere equation: the Hessian determinant balances the source and target densities. Preview that this nonlinear PDE is the analytic heart of Brenier's theorem, met later, and explain each symbol in the ratio.

label: Monotone Coupling on the Line
notes: On the real line the optimal coupling is explicit: push quantiles to quantiles. The increasing rearrangement T equals the target quantile composed with the source distribution function. Emphasize this is the comonotone coupling and it is optimal for every convex cost, a rare closed form we will reuse constantly.

label: Knothe-Rosenblatt Coupling
notes: In higher dimensions the Knothe-Rosenblatt coupling builds a map coordinate by coordinate, conditioning on previous coordinates and applying the one-dimensional monotone rule at each step. It is triangular and explicit but not optimal in general. It is a constructive existence tool and a degeneration limit of optimal maps.

label: The Moriarty Coupling
notes: The Moriarty coupling is Villani's cautionary villain: a coupling engineered to be as bad as possible, spreading mass to maximize cost. It exists for the same reason the good ones do. Use it to stress that the coupling set is large and that optimization, not mere coupling, is what selects structure.

label: Gluing and Recap
notes: Close with the gluing lemma: two couplings sharing a middle marginal can be glued into a joint law on the triple, the device behind the triangle inequality for Wasserstein distance. Then recap the ladder from coupling to plan to map to Jacobian that this chapter has built.
